Logan,

We started seeing intermittent 400-800ms spikes on streaming completions for our longest conversations (context ~18k tokens). Majority of requests return at ~80-120ms, but every ~200th stream arrives late and our UI shows a freeze. We're on the hosted plan, calling via the JS SDK (v1.4.2) with streaming enabled. This is hitting our renewal conversation with the product team — they asked for a mitigation ASAP or we risk delaying the PO. Any quick checks we should run on our side?

Thanks,
Jared

Folks, forwarding Acme Health's samples. TL;DR: intermittent high-latency spikes on streaming responses for long contexts; customer is Hosted and on the renewal path (deal ACME-2027-RENEW-1742). They use JS SDK v1.4.2.

Asking for two things:
1) Short-term mitigation we can offer the customer today (runtime switch, model pin, routing change). They need something low-friction they can apply immediately.
2) Product/SDK ask: expose an explicit client toggle to disable prefetch/prefix-batching behavior (we think the SDK prefetcher + runtime batching may be reordering or delaying initial tokens for long sessions). If feasible, can we scope this as a micro-change (flag in v1.x) rather than a major SDK release?

Attachments: acme_latency_samples.log, sdk-trace-stdout.txt

Logan

Original message from Jared quoted below.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: latency - streaming completions spikes (samples attached)

Thanks for the ping. Quick read of the logs: I see repeated "stream-start" events followed by a long gap before token chunks; patterns align with occasional stall during KV cache population for long prefix lengths. A few notes and immediate suggestions: 

- Can you confirm whether they are using our hosted multi-tenant runtime or have a Dedicated pool? Logan's note says Hosted — if so, we can try routing them to a "low-latency variant" (non-prefetch kernel set) for a limited percentage.
- Short-term mitigation (runtime-only): add a routing rule for ACME CID to prefer model-variant "redwood-gpt-lt-lowlatency" (same weights, different kernel/batching config). This avoids the prefetch path that looks likely to cause the stalls. We can enable for a % of traffic immediately.
- Medium-term: expose an SDK boolean (streaming_prefetch: true/false) that explicitly disables client-side prefetch + prefix batching. We can implement the runtime side to obey a header (x-sdk-streaming-prefetch: 0/1) and have the SDK add it; SDK change should be a patch release if we keep API stable.

Questions for product: Lauren, what is the appetite to add a header-based escape hatch (runtime honors x-sdk-streaming-prefetch) vs. pushing an SDK flag-only rollout? Header-based has the advantage of being scannable in routing/metrics without SDK upgrade. SDK flag is easier for customers but requires release coordination.

I'll prepare a short routing playbook and can toggle variant for Acme in the next maintenance window if we want to trial.

Karthik
Platform / Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: latency - streaming completions spikes (samples attached)

Appreciate the analysis, Karthik. Two thoughts from product perspective: 

1) Header-based escape hatch (x-sdk-streaming-prefetch) seems reasonable as a minimum viable mitigation. It gives immediate operability and doesn't require an SDK release. If runtime can honor it and metrics/telemetry can tag calls, we can roll it to specific accounts and measure the impact.

2) We should still pursue SDK flag in the short roadmap (v1.x patch) so customers who don't control routing can flip it locally. That should be scoped as a small change: expose option in StreamingClient constructor and have the JS/TS SDK set the header. Target: ship in a single minor patch (v1.5.0) if engineering bandwidth allows.

Marissa — from a customer success and sales risk POV, this is high priority because of renewal. Can we coordinate a comms plan? Logan, if we can offer the runtime toggle today, let's tell them the expected window and follow up with a patch timeline.

Lauren
VP Product, Redwood Inference
